articleTitle: Whistler Wave Radiation from a Circular Phased Array of Loop Antennas in a Magnetoplasma
abstract: Radiation from a circular phased array of loop an-tennas in a cold homogeneous magnetoplasma is studied. The emphasis is placed on determining the total radiated power of such an array and its partial powers going to different azimuthal field harmonics in the resonant part of the whistler frequency range. Numerical results are reported for these radiation characteristics under conditions of laboratory experiments with phased arrays of loop antennas in large plasma devices.

articleTitle: Fractional Diffusion-Wave Modification of Landau-Khalatnikov Model Applied to Polarization Switching in Ferroelectric Nanowires
abstract: This paper is devoted to modeling of the diffusion-wave polarization processes in ferroelec-tric nanowires based on time-fractional modification of the Landau-Khalatnikov model. The problem is formalized as an initial-boundary value problem for a semilinear time-fractional partial differential equation. To solve the problem numerically, an implicit computational scheme was derived using the fractional derivative in the Caputo sense. The constructed numerical algorithms were implemented using Matlab software. The designed com-puter program was used to conduct simulations of the spatial-temporal polarization distributions and hysteresis loops for BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanowires in different dynamical modes. This approach allows one to provide modeling of characteristics of polarization processes in low-dimensional ferroelectric systems due to the variation of regimes by means of changes in the dynamical dimension.

articleTitle: Implementing the Peano and WKB Approaches to Find Vibrational Modes and Frequencies of a Thin Rod with Variable Parameters
abstract: The free-bending oscillations of a thin rod under var-ious conditions at its ends are considered. The parameters of stiffness and inertia depend on the longi-tudinal coordinate. The respective solutions to the Bernoulli-Euler equation are obtained using Peano and WKB methods. Dispersion equations are inves-tigated. As shown, the rarely used Peano method is an efficient tool for this problem and allows one to find modes and frequencies. The comparison demonstrates that the WKB method predicts frequencies satisfactorily even by the leading order term, but it is inaccurate in calculating modes. The Peano approach can be used to calculate rod made of functionally graded material with variable Young's mod-ulus and mass density, and also with variable pro-files. Numerical examples are presented in the context of practical assessment of the strength loss in an experimental study of alloys subjected to cyclic point loading at the resonance of bending vibrations.

articleTitle: Miniature Mobius Strip Inspired Scatterer
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a novel subwavelength scatterer, the layout of which is inspired by the Mo-bius strip. The characteristic size of the proposed particle is about 10 mm. So that we consider the frequency range from 1 to 30 GHz in numerical simulation for field distribution calculation of scattering task using finite element method. The results of spectral analysis of multipolar coefficients of far electric field allows us to conclude that with certain specified geometric parameters of the scatterer, co-directional electric and magnetic dipole moments are simultaneously excited in it. Due to this behav-ior at multiple frequencies, the proposed particle is transparent to one circular polarization, while the other is effectively scattered. Due to the reciprocity principle, such scatterer can also be used as an an-tenna with a predictable radiation pattern in several frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Some New Results of Applying the Separation of Variables Method to Spheroids
abstract: Recently, the exact solution to the classical problem of light scattering by a spheroid was extended to diffraction parameters larger than 200. That solution utilized the extended boundary condition method with a sophisticated spheroidal basis, equivalent to use of both Debye potentials and those involved to solve the problem for infinite cylin-ders. In this paper, we combine this approach with the separation of variables method to obtain the same T-matrix in a different, potentially simpler and faster, way. We compare the two solutions concerning their applicability to large scale calculations.

articleTitle: On the Scattering Problem for the Nonhomogeneous Ultrahyperbolic Equation
abstract: Our goal is to set up a well-posed problem for the nonhomogeneous ultrahyperbolic equation in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^{d}\times \mathbb{R}^{n}$</tex>. We focus on the case when a solution is subject to some conditions prescribing its asymp-totic behavior at the infinity. It turns out that such a problem can be formulated in the case of vector-valued solutions. Although the components of a solution are independent in the equation itself, they are intertwined in the asymptotic condition.

articleTitle: Anomalously High Diffraction Efficiency of Low-Frequency Shallow Sinusoidal and Lamellar Gratings for Neutron Optics
abstract: Using commercial codes PCGrate™ and GSolver™, created on the basis of various methods of rigorous electromagnetic theory of diffraction, numerical simulations of the absolute efficiency of low-frequency shallow sinusoidal and lamellar gratings designed to reflect beams of cold neutrons were carried out. It is shown with an inaccuracy of ~ 0.1% that the maximum achiev-able first-order absolute efficiency of sinusoidal and lamellar diffraction gratings can significantly exceed, by 38.5% and 13.7%, the known analytical estimates for these types of profiles, ~ 33.8% and ~ 40.5%, respectively.

articleTitle: Guided Waves and Resonance Effects in Piezoelectric Laminate Structures
abstract: Piezoelectrically generated surface and pseudosurface acoustic waves are simulated and analyzed in the mathematical framework based on the integral representations and guided wave asymptotics, derived using the residue technique. This semi-analytical scheme has been implemented for electri-cally coupled piezomaterials of arbitrary anisotropy. It is illustrated by numerical examples of analyzing wave processes in diamond-based SAW (surface acoustic waves) devices. As a special case, the inter-esting effect of backward SH modes caused by the piezo effect is considered, and the manifestation of the associated ZGV (zero group velocity) resonances and mode repulsions is analyzed.

articleTitle: On the Inverse Dynamic Problem for the First-Order Dissipative System
abstract: We consider the inverse dynamic problem for the first-order dissipative system. We recover the unknown complex potential matrix from the dynamic response (Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator) of the system for positive and negative times.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Inspection of Fluid-Loaded Anisotropic Laminate Plates
abstract: Mathematical and computer models for the interaction of source-generated acoustic wave fields with a multilayer isotropic plate immersed in an acoustic fluid have been developed (Glushkov, Glushkova, Miakisheva, 2019, Ultrasonics, 92, 158-168; Glushkov, Glushkova, Ermolenko, 2022, Russ. J. Nondestruct. Test., 58, 666–678). The aim of this work is to extend these models to the anisotropic case and to analyze wave processes on this basis.

articleTitle: Source Energy Distribution and Wave Energy Streamlines in an Elastic Anisotropic Half-Space
abstract: The time-averaged wave energy supplied by a time-harmonic surface source in an elastic half-space is distributed among the excited surface and body waves. Similar to the isotropic case, the energy partition is calculated using explicit integral and asymp-totic representations in terms of Green's matrix of the substrate and the source parameters. In this paper, after a brief description of the mathematical framework, we discuss the effect of anisotropy on the radiation patterns, source energy partitioning, and wave energy fluxes, illustrating it with several numerical examples.

articleTitle: Unidirectional Pulses. A Short Overview
abstract: A brief overview of the current state of the theory of unidirectional pulses is given.

articleTitle: Guided Wave Propagation Control in Multilayered Piezoelectric Waveguide by System of Electrodes Connected via Electrical Circuits
abstract: The boundary integral equation method to simulate elastic guided waves excited by surface loads in a bimorph plate, which is a three-layer piezoelectric-elastic laminate, with a system of surface electrodes connected through electrical circuits, is discussed. This method is compared with the finite element method to verify its accuracy and efficiency. It provides a useful tool for analyzing the effect of electri-cal circuit's parameters on guided wave propagation in bimorph plates.

articleTitle: Inverse Extremal Problem for an Anti-Tumor Therapy Model
abstract: An optimal control problem for a model of tumor growth is studied. In a given subdomain, it is required to minimize the density of tumor cells, while the drug concentration in tissue is limited by given minimal and maximal values. On the basis of the obtained estimates of the solution to the controlled system, the solvability of the control problem is proved. The problem is reduced to an optimal control problem with a penalty. An algorithm for solving the op-timal control problem with a penalty is constructed and implemented. The efficiency of the algorithm is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Non-Uniqueness in the Water Wave Problem for Partially Submerged Bodies and a Floating Ice Plate
abstract: In this work we study a two-dimensional linear problem describing time-harmonic oscillations of an ideal incompressible fluid of infinite depth in the presence of partially submerged fixed bodies and an ice plate covering part of the fluid surface. The ice is assumed to behave like a thin elastic plate. Examples of solutions of the homogeneous problem (so-called trapped modes) are constructed using a semi-inverse procedure. The scheme is based on the use of the Green function and x-dipole. Their representations, convenient for analysis and numerical implementation, are given.

articleTitle: Solutions to Difference Riccati Equation via Continued Fractions
abstract: We study a difference Riccati equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi(x)+ \rho(x)/\Phi(x-\omega)=v(x)$</tex> with 1-periodic continuous co-efficients. Using continued fraction theory, we inves-tigate a problem of existence of continuous solutions for this equation. It is shown that convergence of a continued fraction representing a solution of the Riccati equation can be expressed in terms of hyperbolicity of a cocycle naturally associated to this continued fraction. We apply the critical set method to establish the uniform hyperbolicity of the cocycle and to obtain sufficient conditions for the convergence of a continued fraction giving a representation for a solution of the Riccati equation.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic Characteristics of a Multigap Loop Antenna with Phased Excitation Located on the Surface of an Anisotropic Cylinder
abstract: We study the electrodynamic characteristics of a multigap loop antenna located on the surface of a circular anisotropic cylinder that is surrounded by a homogeneous isotropic background medium. A closed-form expression for the antenna current, which is excited by appropriately phased external voltages applied across the gaps of the antenna conductor, is found using the integral equation method. Based on the derived current distribution, radiation characteristics of such an antenna are analyzed and its capability of selectively exciting waves with given azimuthal indices is discussed.

articleTitle: Spectral Invariants for Schrödinger Operators on Periodic Discrete Graphs
abstract: We consider Schrödinger operators with real periodic potentials on periodic discrete graphs. Their spectrum consists of a finite number of bands. We construct a complete system of the Floquet spectral invariants, which are polynomials in the potential and determined by cycles in the quotient graph from some specific cycle sets. This system can be used to study the sets of isospectral periodic potentials for the Schrödinger operators on periodic graphs.

articleTitle: Axisymmetric Vibrations of a Cylindrical Elastic Shell with Inhomogeneous Poisson's Ratio
abstract: The problems of design and operation of various pipelines, supports, structural elements, which are modeled by inhomogeneous cylindrical shells, re-main relevant for modern industry. The paper an-alyzes a shell whose inhomogeneous elastic parameters depend on the radial coordinate and these de-pendencies can be described by piecewise continuous functions. Free harmonic vibrations of the shell are considered. Using the example of a two-layer shell with inhomogeneity of Poisson's ratio, the applica-bility area of various models for averaging inhomo-geneous parameters of the shell is analyzed. The influence of inhomogeneity on the shell natural fre-quencies for axisymmetric modes is investigated on the basis of an exact analytical solution.

articleTitle: Hybrid Semi-Analytical Method for Modelling In-Plane Wave Motion of Elastic Structures with Unit-Cells Composed of Waveguides and Joints
abstract: The paper presents a hybrid approach based on the spectral finite element method and the semi-analytical finite element method. The proposed hybrid approach simulates in-plane wave motion of an elastic structure consisting of an elongated layered waveguide of finite length and an adjacent domain of complex shape. The presented semi-analytical hybrid method provides a tool for parametric analysis, where amplitudes of guided waves propagating in elongated part are directly determined.

articleTitle: Surface Waves Generation by a Thin Wire in the Presence of Impedance Surface of Metallic Grid
abstract: In this paper we study excitation of the electromag-netic surface wave by a thin metallic wire of finite length in the presence of impedance surface of metal-lic grid. The wire is located close to the grid and is excited by an incident plane electromagnetic wave. The grid screen is a very dense mesh of a set of infinitely long metallic parallel wires and described by the well-known impedance boundary conditions. Firstly, we demonstrate that the resonances of the thin wire electric current excitation are dramatically enhanced by the presence of impedance surface of metallic grid. Secondly, we describe behaviour of the resonance excitation of the surface waves gener-ated by excitation wire when it is located close to the impedance surface.

articleTitle: Scattering of Surface Waves by Linear Discontinuities in Elastic Half-Space: Approximate Approach
abstract: A point harmonic source of the wave field is located on the surface of an elastic homogeneous half-space with a trench of a rectangular section. The trench in an elastic medium affects the propagation of surface waves, generating scattering wave fields. The source of the wave field and an observation point are located at the opposite sides of a trench. Novel approximate method of calculation of the wave field behind the trench is put forward.

articleTitle: Inverse Problem for a Quasilinear Model of Complex Heat Transfer with Internal Thermal Radiation
abstract: An inverse problem for quasilinear equations of complex heat transfer with power nonlinearity is consid-ered. The problem consists of finding the intensity of internal sources using an integral overdetermination. The global solvability of the problem is proven. The uniqueness of the solution to the problem under the assumption of the boundedness of the temperature gradient is established. An algorithm for solving the inverse problem is constructed and implemented.

articleTitle: On Cylindrically Symmetrical Exact Transparent Boundary Condition in Cylindrical Computational Domain
abstract: Numerical solution of the 3D parabolic equation with any finite-difference scheme requires an appropriate (e.g. transparent or absorbing) boundary condition to truncate the computational domain. Previ-ously, we obtained such an exact transparent bound-ary condition (TBC) in the rectangular computational domain. It should be noted that there exists a class of problems with cylindrical symmetry, for which the use of full TBC in the rectangular domain will lead to unnecessary computational costs. On the other hand, the exact TBC in the circular computational domain, while well known, is formu-lated in quite a complicated form requiring evaluation of complex kernels containing Hankel functions. In this work we demonstrate how the known exact TBC in the rectangular computational domain can be simplified in the presence of cylindrical symme-try and a computationally efficient exact TBC for the cylindrically symmetrical problem in the circu-lar computational domain can be obtained. Further-more, using a number of numerical experiments, we demonstrate how the derived TBC works in practice.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Two Gradient-Based Approaches to Inverse Problem of Ultrasound Tomography
abstract: In the article, we made a comparative analysis of gradient methods for solving the coefficient inverse problem of 2D acoustic tomography. The nonlinear inverse problem is reduced to minimizing the cost functional by two gradient-based methods. Each iteration of the descent requires the solution of direct and adjoint problem. A comparative analysis of the methods is demonstrated based on the results of nu-merical calculations.

articleTitle: An Improved Numerical Algorithm for the Wave Equation Optimization Problems
abstract: A refined algorithm for solving optimization tasks, including direct wave equation problems, is suggested. This method combines the accuracy of classical predecessors with the speed provided by graph-ical processors and modern numerical optimization tools like genetic algorithms and Bayes optimization. The approach is applied to two optimization problems: maximizing the responsivity of quan-tum cascade detectors and the transmitted energy of diffraction gratings. It considers one-periodical gratings with separated interfaces between materi-als of arbitrary conductivity and detectors based on AlGaAs/GaAs and InGaAs/AlInAs materials. The boundary integral equation method is used for the Helmholtz equation, and the symmetrical transfer matrix approach is used for the stationary Schrödiriger- equation. The refined optimization method significantly reduces computation time and enhances the efficiency of quantum optical devices and diffraction gratings.

articleTitle: Paraxial Wave Propagation Along a Delta Potential
abstract: A simple initial value problem for the Schrödiriger-equation (which is usually called “parabolic equation” in the diffraction theory) with a delta potential localized on a half-line is studied asymptotically for various complex amplitudes of the singularity.
